name: Matthias
overview: Matthias was a male figure known primarily as the candidate chosen to replace Judas Iscariot among the twelve apostles, as recorded in Acts 1:23. Scripture does not provide information about his tribe or other personal details beyond this significant role. His selection highlights the early church's commitment to maintaining the apostolic foundation.
namesAndTitles: The name Matthias means "gift of YHWH," reflecting a divine blessing or endowment. This proper name, noted in Acts 1:23, underscores the spiritual significance attributed to him as a chosen apostolic figure.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Matthias beyond his identification as a candidate to replace Judas Iscariot in the twelve apostles. No additional familial or relational details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Matthias matters in the biblical narrative as the individual selected to uphold the integrity of the apostolic twelve after Judas Iscariot's betrayal and departure. His appointment signifies the early church's reliance on divine guidance to preserve the witness and mission entrusted to the apostles. This choice reflects the importance of continuity and faithfulness in the leadership of the nascent Christian community.
